Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg
bär-tō-lō'mä-oos tsē'gên-bälk
n. (Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg, 1682–1719, Halle Pietist, first Protestant missionary to India, at Tranquebar from 1706)
Greek Bartholomaios, son of Talmai; German Ziegenbalg, goatskin.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg was a Halle student sent with Heinrich Plütschau by Frederick IV of Denmark to the Danish settlement at Tranquebar on the Coromandel coast, landing in July 1706 as the first Protestant missionaries to India. The Danish authorities on the spot opposed them and imprisoned Ziegenbalg for four months. He learned Tamil by sitting on the floor of a school with the children, compiled a Tamil grammar and dictionary, translated the New Testament into Tamil by 1711 and most of the Old before his death at thirty-six, set up a press, founded schools for boys and for girls, and wrote careful studies of South Indian religion based on reading its own texts — work Halle suppressed as unnecessary. He insisted the church be Tamil, with Tamil preachers and Tamil hymns. Isa 55:11 is the promise behind the translation. Rev 7:9 the end he worked toward. Act 17:11 the practice he taught his converts.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a missionary as one sent to propagate religion; and vernacular, as native; belonging to the country of one's birth.

MIS'SIONARY, n. One sent to propagate religion.

VERNAC'ULAR, a. Native; belonging to the country of one's birth. We say, the vernacular tongue.

GRAM'MAR, n. The art of speaking or writing a language with propriety, according to established usage.

Modern Corruption

He sat on a schoolroom floor with Tamil children until he could translate the New Testament, and died at thirty-six.

expand to see more

Ziegenbalg settled, in 1706, questions the missionary movement kept relitigating for two centuries. Should the Scriptures be put into the vernacular as a first priority? He did it within five years of landing. Should converts be formed into a church with their own ministers and their own hymns, or kept as dependents? He trained Tamil catechists from the start. Should a missionary study the religion he is addressing? He read the Tamil texts and wrote two books on them, which his own sponsors declined to print, judging that the business was to uproot error and not describe it.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Halle's refusal to publish his studies was the error, and the correction is Act 17, where Paul reads Athens before he preaches to it. Act 17:11 then shows what the converts do with the text once they have it. Rev 7:9 is the warrant for a church that is Tamil and not German: the multitude before the throne is of all kindreds and tongues, and the tongues are not erased on the way in.
